title: Family
final_note: You worked through the key terms in Family.

concepts.def: Smart (2007): focus on chosen relationships including friends, pets and ex-partners as part of personal life.
Giddens (1992): modern relationships continue only while both partners feel rewarded; couples renegotiate continually.
Giddens: love based on equality and openness rather than romantic destiny; reflects late modern reflexivity.
Beck and Beck-Gernsheim (1995): family relationships negotiated rather than ascribed by tradition; risk and freedom rise.
Bott (1957): segregated vs joint roles; influenced by network density.
Smart and May (2010): individuals embedded in networks of family connections that shape choices and identities.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Family — a core area of GCSE Sociology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Family brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Family.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.
